purpose: Narrow DELIVERY successor candidate for Rust protocol v2. It preserves v1 child cardinality, launch, offline lifecycle and non-residency while supplying an exhaustive ordered composite-outcome reducer and host-contextual optional/required D9 v1.13 projection. It does not edit delivery.v2.json.

dependencyPins.use: existing sidecar, offline-bundle, platform and termination-integration authority
exact not-applied D9 vocabulary, derivation, golden axes and class-to-exit map
independent PASS for the exact D9 v1.13 candidate bytes

protocolReference.applicationRule: The protocol, both joins, response and retained checker become usable only after exact-byte independent review and formal application together.

keyFields: complete closed recursively validated resolved-inputs rust-v1 value
workerCardinality.keyComparison: exact recursive value equality; no digest-only, prefix, providerVersion-only or private cache key

processModel.start: After AttemptRecord, sealed Snapshot, verified PlanId, selected rust-v1 universe, exact repository-resolution projection, byte-bearing prepared corpus and admitted Rust stages exist, start one child immediately before the first selected Rust stage. Earlier start is forbidden.
processModel.stageSharing: One Analyze carries all and only selected Rust semantic stages for this exact key in verified ExecutionPlan order.
processModel.end: After every semantic terminal, cancellation, protocol/process/delivery fault, close pipes, terminate the child process group/job if live, reap every owned descendant, erase snapshot/prepared VFS and private scratch, and forget compiler/provider state before supervisor return.
processModel.tcbPosture: Provider, pinned compiler and explicitly granted pre-Plan preparation tools are TCB-accepted. Process separation contains crashes; it is not a security sandbox.
processModel.pureCoreExclusion: Child and supervisor are outside the lifetime-neutral pure core.

host: handshake, identity, limits, schema, sequence, snapshot, prepared-blob and domain validation
ownership.repositoryExecutionOwner: host resolved-inputs adapter after Snapshot seal and before PlanId; all preparation activity terminates before semantic child start

launch.executable: absolute digest-verified path of signed rust-provider artifact; no PATH or shell
launch.argvRule: Exactly six ordered elements; placeholders are host-resolved absolute paths. No response file, extra argument, shell expansion or project-controlled value.

stdio.stdin: fresh unidirectional pipe; protocol frames only
stdio.stdout: fresh unidirectional pipe; protocol frames only through EOF
stdio.stderr: fresh bounded diagnostic byte pipe; never authority

roots.toolchainRoot: read-only verified extraction; every selected component contained and digest-checked
roots.scratchRoot: fresh private bounded host-owned directory, never evidence/cache authority, erased at end
roots.snapshot: transferred sealed VFS only; no live worktree/repository root
roots.preparedOutputs: transferred byte-bearing blobs and mounted read-only sealed VFS only; no CAS, external root, callback or sidecar

preSpawnChecks: signed profile contains exact provider/toolchain artifacts
platform is one of DELIVERY's supported rows
provider/toolchain paths are absolute and contained
Snapshot/PlanId/domain/prepared manifest are complete and verified

diagnosticsAndScratchBounds.stderrOverflow: Capture first bound and a host-owned truncation marker; stderr never supplies semantic or D9 authority.

d9Reference.rule: Exact values are cross-derived from the hash-pinned v1.13 bytes. This join neither applies v1.13 nor changes DELIVERY's current binding.

providerObservationV2.rule: A provider terminal is validated as an observation first. Unavailable and BudgetExhausted carry exhaustive unknown Coverage and their protocol deficiency spelling, but do not decide whether the provider was required, whether a C-1 predicate remains sufficient, or the public D9 result.

fields.firstEleven: exact booleans; booleans are independent observations and composites are permitted

compositeObservationV2.domainCalculation: 2^11 boolean assignments times 6 terminalKind values; the checker enumerates every tuple
compositeObservationV2.note: coverageObserved deliberately remains independent so Coverage+hang is an explicit composite.

orderedNormalizationReducerV2.evaluation: Evaluate rows by ascending priority and return immediately on the first true predicate. Exactly one normalizedFate is returned; later true predicates are observations only, never additional fates.
orderedNormalizationReducerV2.equalPublicCodeRule: POST_TERMINAL_OUTPUT, MALFORMED_FRAME, SCHEMA_OR_COMMITMENT_FAULT, HANDSHAKE_MISMATCH, DEADLINE_HANG, NONZERO_EXIT, EARLY_EOF, UNSOLICITED_CANCELLED, PROVIDER_DECLARED_FAULT and INCOMPLETE_PROTOCOL all later project to provider-protocol, but remain mutually single normalized fates. Equal D9 code never licenses multiple reducer results.
orderedNormalizationReducerV2.totalityRule: All 12288 finite input tuples return exactly one listed fate; no fallthrough, exception, multiple output, local priority or timeout-as-budget branch is allowed.

fields.admittedProviderRequiredness: optional|required; required includes C-2 contribution role required or blocking and an explicitly required stage/provider postcondition
fields.c1PredicateSufficiencyWithoutProvider: sufficient|insufficient; computed per admitted C-1 predicate/relation/rung against all non-provider Coverage, never as a provider-global boolean

hostFinalizerContextV2.custody: All fields are host-derived after provider observation validation. The provider cannot supply, default or override them.

order: If interruptionTiming=signal-before-finalization or normalizedFate=USER_INTERRUPTED, use the exact interrupted row regardless of simultaneous provider/process faults.
If interruptionTiming=signal-after-finalization, preserve the already settled finalization result.
Operational normalized fates map without semantic deficiency.
For verified semantic fates, derive effectiveProviderRequired and apply the contextual rows below.
Pass the resulting complete axes through the exact hash-pinned D9 v1.13 reference derivation and classToExitCode; do not write a provider-local code.

rows.providerEffect: introduces no provider deficiency; final class/exit derives from host Coverage, verdict, durability and postconditions

rows.otherwise: provider adds no deficiency; exact D9 derivation uses the host's non-provider axes

rows.requiredConditionsForExactGolden: durability=committed and requiredPostconditions=met; a host durability/postcondition failure takes its higher-priority exact D9 operational path

rows.providerEffect: provider adds no primary deficiency because all admitted C-1 predicates remain sufficiently evidenced; exact D9 derives from remaining host axes

rows.requiredConditionsForExactGolden: durability=committed and requiredPostconditions=met; a host durability/postcondition failure takes its higher-priority exact D9 operational path

rows.rule: A legal Cancel originates in the user-interrupt path and therefore normally matches the first row; if finalization was already committed, preserve that settled result rather than reclassify it.

hostFinalizerProjection.c1PredicateRelativeRule: Sufficiency is evaluated for every admitted consumer predicate against its required relation and minimum rung. Optional provider identity alone never implies optional evidence; conversely provider unavailability is not a deficiency when other admitted Coverage already satisfies every predicate.
hostFinalizerProjection.observationFirstRule: Unavailable/BudgetExhausted is recorded and Coverage validated before this projection. Rewriting the wire terminal based on requiredness or letting a terminal directly select deficiency/class/exit is forbidden.
hostFinalizerProjection.conditionalApplicationRule: These rows cross-derive exact v1.13 candidate values only. They do not apply v1.13 to DELIVERY or product code.

exhaustivenessRule: The ordered reducer assigns one normalized fate to every composite observation; then exactly one operational/interruption/semantic finalizer branch owns it. No equal-code merging, multiple-match output, implementation-local exit status, partial Coverage seal or timeout-as-budget rule is permitted.
residuals: Formal application to DELIVERY and formal application of D9 v1.13 remain outside this candidate.
Independent review must replay all 12288 reducer tuples and exact D9 golden cross-derivations.
Product implementation, process-tree behavior, network-disabled preparation, platforms and release evidence remain unexecuted.
